answer: Require each agent identity to be bound to one hardware attestation, as unique as a basalt fingerprint: a device can issue only one credential, and that credential must lock a time-delayed bond. Creating a thousand fake agents then needs a thousand devices and a thousand bonds, so the attacker cost grows linearly instead of once. If two identities share an attestation, like the same pigment reused in a forgery, or water carving one karst channel, both bonds are slashed and both identities are removed.
